newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian police arrest leading Mafia boss.
newsitem.headline: Italian police arrest leading Mafia boss.

text.p: Police said on Saturday they had arrested fugitive gangster Girolamo Mole, one of Italy's most-wanted Mafia bosses.
The 36-year-old Mole, nicknammed "Mommo", was seized early on Saturday near the town of Gioia Tauro in the southwest Calabria region.
He is considered a top boss of Calabria's 'Ndrangheta mafia and among Italy's 30 most-wanted criminals.
Mole had been on the run since June 1993 when the first of eight arrest warrants was issued against him on charges ranging from Mafia association and murder to extortion and various other crimes.
An international arrest warrant had been issued against him in December 1995.
Police in Reggio Calabria were expected to give further details at a news conference later on Saturday.
News of the arrest came after police said they had smashed two organised crime rings in dawn swoops in Calabria and Sicily, arresting scores of suspected mobsters.

Some 50 people were arrested in Calabria on suspicion of running a heroin ring in Reggio Calabria and 15 others were held in connection with an investigation into the Mafia's virtual stranglehold over the ship-building industry in Palermo.
Both operations came a day after the government approved a plan to send 500 troops to Naples to help police crack down on gangsters who are plaguing the southern port with turf wars.
